topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Therapy
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class to the final lecture and introduces the learning objectives regarding cancer treatment modalities and their mechanisms.

topics.label: Traditional Modalities: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover conventional cancer treatments that physically remove or non-specifically damage rapidly dividing cells, along with their associated side effects and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cellular Vulnerabilities and DNA Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer therapies can exploit specific cell cycle checkpoint failures, hormone dependencies, and defective DNA repair pathways for selective cell killing.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction, Kinase Inhibitors, and Resistance Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the identification of driver oncogenes and detail the design, clinical implementation, and emergence of resistance and addiction to small-molecule kinase inhibitors.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how therapeutic antibodies are engineered to target tumor cell-surface antigens directly or deliver cytotoxic payloads selectively.

topics.label: Immunotherapy and T-Cell Engagement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore immune surveillance and describe approaches to harness and engineer T cells against tumors, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic Challenges, Historical Progress, and Future Directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the systemic challenges in cancer management, evaluate historical survival trends, and consider future directions and clinical dilemmas in cancer treatment.
